extracted.intended_audience: scholars and editors preparing/reviewing scholarly reprints of early-modern English texts
extracted.subtask_short: editing reprints of early English texts
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and practice notes for producing a scholarly reprint of an early-modern English work, including choices about base-text selection, collation, orthography, variant marking, and documentation of manuscript sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Text base and collation
rubrics_metrics.description: The text has been taken from the edition of 1732, collated with the first impression in 1628.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a later reliable edition as the base-text but collate it carefully with the earliest (first) impression; record where the two differ and use the collation to identify additions, alterations, and original-first-edition readings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variant marking convention
rubrics_metrics.description: Those words or passages which have been added since the first edition are contained between brackets, [and printed in the common type]; those which have received some alteration, are printed in _italic_, and the passages, as they stand in the first edition, are always given in a note.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt explicit typographic conventions to mark types of variants: brackets for post-first-edition additions, italics for altered readings, and notes (footnotes/endnotes) to present the first-edition text. Make the convention clear in a front-matter statement so readers can interpret variants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of emendation (conservative emendation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reprinted, without altering any thing but the plain errors of the press, and the old pointing and spelling in some places.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emend only manifest printing errors and selectively update obsolete pointing/orthography; avoid substantive alteration of the text beyond obvious press mistakes—preserve the character of the historical text unless correction is necessary and defensible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orthography policy for main text and appendix
rubrics_metrics.description: I have retained in this Appendix the spelling I found. Bliss's text has, with a few exceptions (possibly accidental), the modern spelling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State and apply a consistent policy on orthography: retain original spellings in documentary appendices or where fidelity is required; modernize spelling in the main text only where indicated and note exceptions. Make transparent which parts preserve original orthography and which are modernized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial responsibility and disclaimers
rubrics_metrics.description: For the Notes, Appendix, and Index, the editor is entirely answerable, and although he is fully aware that many superfluities will be censured, many omissions discovered, and many errors pointed out, he hopes that the merits of the original author will, in a great measure, compensate for the false judgment or neglect of his reviver.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state what the editor accepts responsibility for (annotations, appendices, indexes). Acknowledge probable imperfections and invite critical scrutiny while clarifying editorial choices and aims in the front matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation and reporting of manuscript and printed sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Account of the Durham MS. ... printed, besides, some other versions quoted by Bliss from 'Dr. Bright's MS.,' and incorporated in his annotated copy of his own book. I was enabled by the kindness of Dr. Greenwell, the Librarian, to take it away and examine it at leisure; and the courtesy of the University Librarian, Dr. Fowler, furnished me with an exact collation of the MS. versions with the printed text ... I have added a few 'testimonies' to Earle from Anthony Wood and others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record and report all manuscript and printed witnesses used (library locations, collations, which readings come from which source). Where provenance or identity of a manuscript is uncertain, state the uncertainty. Include relevant documentary materials (letters, testimonies) in an appendix and cite the exact sources for readers and future editors.
